title: Properties of the retained localization
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $T\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}R$ a Zariski closed subset, and $R_{[T]}$ the retained localization [def-weil-pbc-retained-localization]. The map $R\to R_{[T]}$ is ind-Zariski [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Its points are precisely the pairs $(x,y)$ of primes of $R$ with $x\in T$ and $y\subseteq x$, and the canonical map from $R_y$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] to the local ring at $(x,y)$ is an isomorphism. If every point of $T$ is closed in $\operatorname{Spec}R$, then $\operatorname{Spec}R_{[T]}$ is w-local [def-weil-pbc-w-local], with closed point set identified with $T$ (with its patch topology). If, under this closed-point hypothesis, $T=V(J)$ for an ideal $J\subseteq R$, then the canonical quotient map $R/J\to R_{[T]}/JR_{[T]}$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Put C=R^w and B=R_[T]. Present C→B as the filtered colimit indexed by constructible supersets of T of the one-factor products C[e_E⁻¹]. The canonical maps identify its colimit with the defining retained algebra. Composition stability with the ind-principal-Zariski presentation of R→C gives R→B ind-principal-Zariski.

For each x in Spec R construct C→R_x by projecting every finite partition stage to its unique part containing x, then localizing. Refinement compatibility follows from uniqueness of localization maps. This map is surjective: represent a/s at the partition D(s), V(s), with denominators s and 1, respectively. The selector e_E maps to 1 if x lies in E and 0 otherwise. The pullback of the maximal prime of R_x is a closed ambient point whose contracted base prime is x. The ambient point theorem makes this the diagonal point in the component with first coordinate x. Since D(e_E) is clopen, membership is constant on that component. Therefore e_E avoids the prime (x,y) if and only if x lies in E.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: selector support, expanded using explicit evaluation maps

proof.text: Each C→C[e_E⁻¹] is surjective because e_E is idempotent. The filtered-colimit representative lemma implies C→B is surjective, so the spectrum map is a closed embedding. Its image consists exactly of primes q avoiding every selector. One inclusion follows because each selector becomes a unit. Conversely the principal localization maps C[e_E⁻¹]→C_q form a cocone; descend it to B→C_q and pull back the maximal prime, whose contraction is q. By the preceding step the image is the primes whose first coordinate lies in every constructible superset of T. This intersection is T: if x is outside T=V(I), choose f in I outside x and use the constructible superset V(f). Restrict the ambient point equivalence to this closed subspace.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: retained prime pairs

proof.text: For any ind-principal-Zariski algebra, the canonical ring map is bijective on stalks. Apply Algebra.BijectiveOnStalks.of_colimitPresentation from the source library to the presentation in step 1. Each stage is a finite product of principal localizations, for which RingHom.BijectiveOnStalks.pi and the standard-open-immersion criterion apply; transport along the stage algebra equivalence. This proves the canonical local-ring isomorphism at each listed retained prime, since its second coordinate is exactly its contraction to R.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: canonical local rings, using the proved source-library stalk API

proof.text: W-locality descends from C to B along the surjection of step 3, by the proved IsWLocalRing.of_surjective. A closed embedding identifies closed points with ambient closed points in its image. Restrict the ambient patch-spectrum-to-closed-points homeomorphism to first coordinates in T; step 3 identifies its range. The restriction is an embedding onto T, hence its inverse gives T homeomorphic to the retained closed-point set. Compatibility with the ambient diagonal proves the stated diagonal formula. In fact this part does not need the closed-point hypothesis on T.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: w-locality and patch closed-point homeomorphism

proof.text: Assume T=V(J) and its points are closed. A prime of B containing JB gives a retained pair (x,y) with J≤y≤x. Then y lies in T and is maximal, so y=x. Restricting the pair equivalence gives a bijection between V(JB) and V(J). Conjugate by the canonical quotient-spectrum equivalences to obtain bijectivity of the spectrum map of the canonical ring map R/J→B/JB. The bijective-on-stalks property of step 4 passes to this quotient map by RingHom.BijectiveOnStalks.quotientMap. The proved source lemma RingHom.BijectiveOnStalks.bijective_of_bijective concludes that this canonical ring map is bijective. Thus no zero-dimensional profiniteness, compact-Hausdorff bijection, or affine homeomorphism criterion is needed.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: canonical quotient isomorphism via the proved source-library stalk criterion

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $R$ be a ring and $J\subset R$ an ideal, and let $R_{[J]}$ be as in
[def-weil-pbc-retained-localization].

1. The map $R\to R_{[J]}$ is ind-Zariski [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], and
   $\operatorname{Spec}R_{[J]}$ is w-local [def-weil-pbc-w-local].
2. If $V(J)$ consists of closed points of $\operatorname{Spec}R$, then the
   closed points of $\operatorname{Spec}R_{[J]}$ are exactly the points of
   $V(JR_{[J]})$, the map $V(JR_{[J]})\to V(J)$ is bijective, and
   $R/J\to R_{[J]}/JR_{[J]}$ is an isomorphism.
3. Let $A$ be a w-local ring, $I\subset A$ an ideal with $V(I)$ the set of closed
   points of $\operatorname{Spec}A$, and $B$ an $A$-algebra such that for every
   prime $\mathfrak q$ of $B$ over a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $A$ the residue
   field extension $\kappa(\mathfrak q)/\kappa(\mathfrak m)$ is algebraic. Then the
   closed points of $\operatorname{Spec}B_{[IB]}$ are exactly the points of
   $V(IB_{[IB]})$. If moreover $A\to B$ is faithfully flat, so is
   $A\to B_{[IB]}$.

proof.text:
*1.* The map $R^w\to R_{[J]}$ is a localization, hence ind-Zariski, and
$R\to R^w$ is ind-Zariski by [lem-weil-pbc-w-localization-points]; compose
using [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability]. The spectrum of $R_{[J]}$ is
identified with the set of points of the w-local space
$\operatorname{Spec}R^w$ that generalize a point of the closed set
$V(JR^w)$. In a w-local space this set is closed, and a closed subspace of a
w-local space is w-local.

*2.* By [lem-weil-pbc-w-localization-points], $V(JR^w)$ maps bijectively to
$V(J)$ and $R/J\cong R^w/JR^w$. A prime of $R^w$ containing $JR^w$ lies over a
maximal ideal of $R$ and has the same residue field, since $R\to R^w$
identifies local rings; as in 3 below it is therefore maximal. These primes survive in
$R_{[J]}$ and are the points of $V(JR_{[J]})$; they are closed, and every
point of $\operatorname{Spec}R_{[J]}$ generalizes one of them, so they are
exactly the closed points. Finally $R^w/JR^w\to R_{[J]}/JR_{[J]}$ is the
localization of $R^w/JR^w$ at elements that are already units, hence an
isomorphism.

*3.* A prime $\mathfrak q$ of $B$ containing $IB$ lies over a maximal ideal
$\mathfrak m$ of $A$; since $B/\mathfrak q$ is a domain containing the field
$\kappa(\mathfrak m)$ whose fraction field is algebraic over it, $B/\mathfrak q$
is a field and $\mathfrak q$ is maximal. So $V(IB)$ consists of closed points
and 2 applies to $J=IB$. If $A\to B$ is faithfully flat, then
$A\to B_{[IB]}$ is flat by 1, and every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\supset I$ of
$A$ is the image of a prime of $B$ containing $IB$, which by 2 is the image
of a point of $\operatorname{Spec}B_{[IB]}$. Since flat maps satisfy going
down and every prime of $A$ lies in a maximal ideal, $\operatorname{Spec}
B_{[IB]}\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is surjective.
